sentences.text: 3. The Claim Case was filed under section 166/140 of the Motor Vehicle Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 3,00,000/- for the injuries and permanent disablement sustained by the injured which was occurred on 10.07.2007 at about 7.30 A.M. at village Hunkarkhap on Bagra Balumath Main Road, P.S. Simariya, District- Ghatra.
On that date Subodh Kumar Yadav was going by his three wheel cycle to market.

When he reached near Hunkarkhap, one truck coming from Balumath Kari Devi vs The New India Assurance Company Limited on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122290576/
1 side, which has been rashly driven rashly and negligently by its driver dashed the cycle of Subodh Kumar Yadav causing injury on his right leg.

sentences.text: He was sent to the hospital and examined.

Thereafter a case was registered in which after investigation police submitted chargesheet under sections 279,
337, 338 of the I.P.C.
4.
The learned Tribunal by the impugned award dated 03.01.2015 has been pleased to allow the claim and awarded Rs. 75,000/-.
Aggrieved with that award, appellant has approached this Court in this appeal for enhancement of the awarded amount.

5. Mr. Vijay Kumar Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned tribunal has not awarded the amount on pain suffering inconvenience and hardship and for mental and physical shock.
On these grounds, he submits that the amount is required to be enhanced.

6. Mr. G.C. Jha, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant-New Assurance Company Ltd.
submits that Subodh Yadav was already disabled person that is why he was travelling on tricycle.

He submits that doctor has examined and found 40% injury which has not been demonstrated by the evidences and 40% disablement was due to taking into earlier disablement also and doctor has not been examined by the appellant.

The contention of Mr. G.C. Jha, has been supported by Mr. K.K.
Singh learned counsel for the respondent no.2 who submits that only a sum of Rs. 8623/- was incurred in treatment expenses however, the learned tribunal has granted Rs. 50,000/- as compensation and there is no illegality in the award.

7. In view of above submission of the learned counsel for the parties the Court has gone through the judgement of the learned tribunal and finds that the learned tribunal has considered the exhibits and evidences on record.

The original disablement certificate no. 025 dated 08.04.2008 -Exhibit X/3 issued by the office of Civil Surgeon, Sadar Hospital, Chatra wherein it has been disclosed that Subodh Kumar Yadav has 40% physical impairment.
He was examined by three doctors.
Since the claimants have not examined any doctor of the board to prove the same, so this certificate was marked as Exhibit X/3.
The tribunal has considered that he was travelling by tricycle as a disabled person.
Thus Subodh Kumar Yadav is a disabled person from the date of accident earlier.
Learned tribunal has considered that treatment expenses was incurred as 8623/- and learned tribunal has granted Rs. 50,000/- including the treatment of expenses of Rs. 8623/-.

In the head of special diet cost of nursing and care, constant attendance, extra diet and nourishment, the claimants are entitled for Rs. 25,000/- and accordingly Rs. 75,000/- was allowed in favour of the claimant.
Due to non-examination of doctor and considering that Subodh Kumar Yadav was disabled persons from earlier also, there is no illegality in the impugned award.
Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed.

( Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Satyarthi/
